title: Practitioner Exam
description: 35 questions covering all five modules, drawn from a pool of 44. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: A finance analyst wants to explore revenue by product line, territory and quarter, drilling from a year into its quarters wherever a figure looks odd.
questions.prompt: Which tool should they build this in?
options: Report Designer
Dashboard Designer
Analyzer
Interactive Reports
questions.explanation: Analyzer is the OLAP tool: it pivots measures across dimensions and drills down a hierarchy such as Years to Quarters with a double-click. Interactive Reports lays out grouped rows and totals from a metadata model rather than drilling through a hierarchy. Dashboard Designer arranges existing content and prompts on one page rather than exploring a cube. Report Designer is a desktop tool for pixel-perfect published reports, not ad-hoc exploration.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: A sales director wants one page showing a geographic analysis, an existing orders report and an inventory list, all filtered by the same Territory selection.
questions.prompt: Which tool builds this page?
options: Interactive Reports
Analyzer
Dashboard Designer
Schema Workbench
questions.explanation: Dashboard Designer places existing Analyzer, Interactive Reporting and Report Designer content in panels and binds one dashboard prompt to each report's parameter. Analyzer builds a single analysis, not a page of several. Interactive Reports builds a single tabular report. Schema Workbench models Mondrian cubes and produces nothing a business user views.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: A regional manager needs a printable list of orders grouped by Territory and Country, with a revenue subtotal for each group and no charts.
questions.prompt: Which tool is the best fit?
options: Interactive Reports
Dashboard Designer
Pentaho Data Integration
Analyzer
questions.explanation: Interactive Reports builds grouped tabular reports with subtotals, and page setup for printing, from a metadata model in the browser. Analyzer pivots and drills a cube, which is more than a fixed grouped list needs. Dashboard Designer arranges existing content rather than building a report. Pentaho Data Integration moves and transforms data; it does not lay out reports.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: The database behind the Orders metadata model moves to a new server. Forty Interactive Reports are built on that model.
questions.prompt: What has to change for the reports to keep working?
options: The data source, re-selected inside each report
Nothing, since each report keeps its own copy of the rows
The saved query in each report, one at a time
Only the database connection the Orders model uses
questions.explanation: The database connection belongs to the metadata model, and every report on the model reaches the database through it, so re-pointing that one connection serves all forty. Reports store a query against the model, not SQL against a server, so there is no saved query to edit report by report. Re-selecting the data source in each report would pick the same model again and change nothing. A saved report holds definitions and no rows, which is why it re-queries every time it opens.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: Regional leads want an orders report in their inbox on the first of every month, and nobody wants to run it by hand.
questions.prompt: What should the report owner set up in the User Console?
options: A Favorite for each lead that points to the report
A monthly schedule for the report that emails its output
A dashboard holding the report, with a refresh interval
A copy of the report in each lead's Home folder
questions.explanation: A schedule runs the report on the server's scheduler at a set recurrence and can email the output, with nobody opening it. A Favorite is a per-user shortcut, so someone still has to open the report. A copy in each Home folder duplicates the definition and still has to be run by hand. A dashboard's refresh interval re-renders panels only while someone has the dashboard open.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Schedules

questions.scenario: A modeller proposes renaming the Territory level of a sales cube to Region, to match new company language. Dozens of analyses and several dashboards use the cube.
questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason to treat this as a reviewed change rather than a quick edit?
options: Mondrian must reload the fact table before the new name appears
Renaming a level resets the cube's measures to a Count aggregation
A cube cannot be republished once reports have been built on it
Saved analyses and dashboards refer to the level by its schema name
questions.explanation: An Analyzer report saves each field as a schema formula such as [Markets].[Territory], and dashboards map parameters to those levels, so a rename reaches every report and link built on the cube; that reach is why models are reviewed and versioned like software. A name is metadata, so no fact table is reloaded; Mondrian generates SQL per query. A cube can be republished at any time, which is exactly what makes an unreviewed change risky. A measure's aggregation is set on the measure and does not change when a level is renamed.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: In one company, business users build their own reports in the browser from governed models. In another, IT builds every report and business users only open them.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes the first approach from the second?
options: Whether the finished reports can be scheduled
Where the data lives, in spreadsheets or databases
Who authors the reports, not which models they use
How current the data is when a report is opened
questions.explanation: Self-service and managed reporting can sit on the same governed models; the difference is that self-service puts authoring in business users' hands, while managed reporting keeps it with IT and delivers finished reports. Both can run on databases, so where the data lives does not separate them. Both re-query when a report opens, so freshness is the same. Reports built either way can be scheduled.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Self-service vs managed reporting

questions.scenario: EMEA managers must see only EMEA rows and NA managers only NA rows in every report built on the Orders model, including reports written next year.
questions.prompt: Where should that restriction be defined?
options: In the repository permissions on each report's own folder
In the Orders model's security, keyed to the user's role
As a Territory prompt defaulting to the user's region
As a Territory filter saved into each report
questions.explanation: Security defined in the metadata model is applied to every query the model generates, so every report on it, including future ones, is restricted by the user's role. A filter saved into each report has to be remembered in every new report, and any author can remove it. A prompt lets the user choose another value. Folder permissions decide who can open a report, not which rows it returns.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: A new analyst has a login to the Pentaho Server and a web browser, and nothing installed on their laptop.
questions.prompt: What can they do from the User Console alone?
options: Build pixel-perfect reports as in Report Designer
Design transformations and jobs on a canvas
Open, create and schedule reports and dashboards
Edit Mondrian schemas as in Schema Workbench
questions.explanation: The User Console is the browser front end of the Pentaho Server: from it users open content, create Interactive Reports, Analyzer reports and dashboards, and schedule them. Transformations and jobs are designed in Spoon, a desktop tool. Mondrian schemas are edited in Schema Workbench, also a desktop tool. Report Designer is a desktop application too.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Pentaho User Console

questions.scenario: An IT manager is choosing between giving 300 business users browser access to the User Console and installing a desktop reporting tool on each laptop.
questions.prompt: Which consideration most favours the browser?
options: Reports run faster in a browser than in any desktop reporting tool
One server upgrade reaches every user, with no clients to update
Browsers can render chart types that desktop tools cannot draw
Browser access removes the need to manage user permissions
questions.explanation: With browser delivery, content, permissions and upgrades live on the server, so one upgrade reaches all 300 users and no laptop drifts out of step. Desktop tools draw charts too, so rendering is not the difference. Permissions still apply, and the server enforces them on every request. Report speed depends on the query and the server, not on the browser.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Pentaho User Console

questions.scenario: An analyst opens an Interactive Report a month after it was saved and sees this morning's orders in it.
questions.prompt: Why does the report show current data?
options: The server refreshes a stored copy of its rows each night
The data source copies its new rows into the report file
The report was scheduled to rebuild itself every day
The saved report holds a query definition and re-runs it
questions.explanation: A saved Interactive Report is a bundle of definitions, the layout plus a query against the model, with no rows, so opening it re-runs the query against current data. No stored copy of rows exists to refresh. A schedule produces output, but opening the report does not depend on one. A report references its data source and never holds a copy of its rows.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Data sources

questions.scenario: A user opened a sales report yesterday but cannot remember which folder it is in, and wants to open it again.
questions.prompt: Where in the User Console will they find it fastest?
options: Administration
Recents
Opened
Schedules
questions.explanation: Recents lists content the user has opened lately, so yesterday's report is one click away without knowing its folder. Schedules lists scheduled runs, not recently viewed content. Opened shows what is open in the current session, and yesterday's report is not. Administration manages users, roles and server settings.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Perspectives

questions.scenario: To keep a confidential report from the Sales role, a consultant removes the link to its folder from a custom portal page, but leaves the folder's permissions unchanged.
questions.prompt: Can a Sales user still open the report?
options: Yes, from any client, because the folder's permissions allow it
No, because content with no link to it cannot be requested
Only once an administrator shares the report with them again
No, because the portal page now controls access to the folder
questions.explanation: The server checks the requested content's access-control list on every request, and the folder still grants Sales access, so the User Console, Report Designer, a script or the REST API can all fetch the report. Content needs no link to be requested; any client can ask the server for a path. A portal page is one client among many and holds no permissions. Nothing was unshared, so there is nothing to share again; changing the folder's permissions is what would stop them.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Users & Roles

questions.scenario: An analyst has finished a report the whole sales team will run each week, and has a draft of another report that is not ready to share.
questions.prompt: Where should each be saved?
options: Team report in a shared Public folder, draft in their Home folder
Team report in their Home folder, draft in a shared Public folder
Both in their Home folder, with the folder shared to the sales team
Both in a shared Public folder, with the draft renamed
questions.explanation: Content in a shared Public folder can be found and run by others, subject to the folder's permissions, while a Home folder is personal space, so the draft stays private until it is ready. Sharing a Home folder makes team content depend on one person's private space. Renaming a draft in Public still exposes it to everyone with access. The reverse arrangement publishes the draft and hides the finished report.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Browse Files

questions.scenario: An orders report with a Row Limit of 100 shows a plausible subtotal for its first territory, but later territories are missing or far too small, and no error appears.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: The later territories have no orders in the chosen date range
Subtotals are computed only for the first page of output
The summary function was set to Average instead of Sum
The query stopped at 100 rows, so the totals cover only those
questions.explanation: A row limit is applied in the query, so the database returns only the first 100 rows in sort order and the summaries add up only what arrived; set the limit to Maximum before trusting a total. Subtotals run over every row returned, not just the first page. Missing orders would hit territories at random, not everything after the first. Average would change every subtotal's value, not make later territories disappear.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Query settings

questions.scenario: A report grouped by Territory lists one row per order line, and the manager wants each territory's subtotal to show how many different orders it contains.
questions.prompt: Which summary should be set on Order Number?
options: Count Distinct
Maximum
Count
Sum
questions.explanation: Count Distinct counts each order number once, however many lines the order has. Count counts rows, so an order with five lines is counted five times. Sum adds the order numbers themselves, which means nothing. Maximum returns only the highest order number in the group.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Totals

questions.scenario: Each territory manager wants the same orders report showing only their own territory, and the author wants to maintain a single report.
questions.prompt: What should the author add to the report?
options: A calculated field that returns each manager's territory
A prompt on Territory, so the value is chosen at run time
A group on Territory, so each manager scrolls to their own
A filter on Territory, set to each manager's value in turn
questions.explanation: A prompt is a filter whose value arrives at run time, so one report serves every territory, and schedules and dashboards can set the same parameter. A fixed filter serves one territory at a time, so it would need a copy per manager. A group shows every territory in one report instead of restricting it to one. A calculated field cannot be used as a filter or prompt at all.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Prompts

questions.scenario: A wide grouped report looks fine in the browser, but when it is exported to PDF its rightmost columns spill onto separate pages.
questions.prompt: Which change fixes the exported layout?
options: Raise the Row Limit to Maximum
Export the report as CSV instead of PDF
Turn on Sticky HTML header rows
Switch to landscape in Page Setup
questions.explanation: Page Setup controls page format, orientation and margins, and the default is Letter portrait, so landscape gives the columns room on each page. Sticky HTML header rows freeze the header in HTML output only. The Row Limit controls how many rows come back, not how wide a page is. CSV drops the layout entirely, so it avoids the problem rather than fixing the PDF.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Page setup

questions.scenario: The NA and EMEA sales teams each want an orders report that differs only in territory, delivered monthly to their own recipients.
questions.prompt: Which approach is easiest to maintain?
options: One report per team, copied each month from a master
One report with a Territory prompt, one schedule per team
Two reports, each with its own territory filter fixed in it
One report grouped by Territory, sent to both teams
questions.explanation: One prompted report is a single definition, and each schedule sets the Territory parameter for its team, so a layout change is made once. Two fixed reports double every future change. A grouped report sends each team the other team's data. Copying from a master each month repeats the work and lets the copies drift.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Orders NA and EMEA

questions.scenario: An analyst adds Customer Name, Order Date and Total to an Interactive Report. The three fields come from three different tables in the database.
questions.prompt: How is the join between those tables worked out?
options: The analyst picks the join keys as each field is added
The database infers the join from matching column names
The metadata layer follows relationships defined in the model
Interactive Reports joins the rows together in the user's browser
questions.explanation: Relationships between business tables are defined once in the metadata model, and the metadata layer walks them to generate one SQL statement with the right joins. The analyst never names a key column; that is the point of the model. The join happens in the generated SQL, in the database, not in the browser. Databases do not infer joins from column names; the SQL has to state them.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Metadata model

questions.scenario: An analyst adds a calculated field, Tax = [Total] * 0.15, to an Interactive Report, then tries to filter to orders where Tax is over 1,000 and finds the option unavailable.
questions.prompt: Why can the calculated field not be filtered?
options: The expression has to be written in SQL before it can filter
Calculated fields must be published before they can filter
The report engine computes it after the query has returned
Filters accept only fields that already have a prompt
questions.explanation: A calculated field is a formula the reporting engine evaluates row by row after the data arrives, so the database never sees it and there is nothing for a WHERE clause to use; the same expression defined as a formula column in the metadata model would filter, sort and aggregate. No publish step enables filtering. Filters work on ordinary fields with or without a prompt. Interactive Reports takes no SQL expressions; the fix is the model, not a different syntax.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Computed fields

questions.scenario: A report is filtered to one territory, grouped by Country, and sorted by Customer Name. The author wonders how the rows arrive in group order.
questions.prompt: How are the rows put in order for the groups to work?
options: The groups are formed first, and the filter is applied after
Group fields go into the query's ORDER BY ahead of the column sort
The report engine re-sorts all of the returned rows in memory by group
The column sort is applied first, and the groups follow it
questions.explanation: The engine starts a new group when a value changes between consecutive rows, so group fields are placed ahead of any column sort in the query's ORDER BY and the database does the ordering, while the filter goes into the WHERE clause. Nothing is re-sorted in memory, which is why large reports group without extra memory. The filter runs in the database before any rows reach the engine. A column sort ahead of the groups would break them, which is why group keys always sort first.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Filtering & sorting

questions.scenario: A finance system accepts only delimited text files, and the regional director wants a fixed-layout copy of the same report to print for a board meeting.
questions.prompt: Which two export formats meet those needs?
options: CSV
PDF
Excel
HTML
PowerPoint (PPTX)
questions.explanation: CSV is delimited text the finance system can load, and PDF keeps a fixed page layout for printing. HTML is built for viewing in a browser, where page layout and printing depend on the browser. Excel produces a workbook, not delimited text. PowerPoint (PPTX) is not an Interactive Reports output at all; the formats are HTML, PDF, CSV and Excel.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Output formats

questions.scenario: A sales manager wants an orders report covering only the Motorcycles and Planes product lines, with Quantity Ordered subtotalled for each product line within each territory.
questions.prompt: Which report design meets this?
options: Filter Product Line to the two lines, then sort by Territory and then Product Line
Prompt for Product Line, then group by Territory and then Product Line
Filter Product Line to the two lines, then group by Product Line and then Territory
Filter Product Line to the two lines, then group by Territory and then Product Line
questions.explanation: The filter keeps only the two product lines, and nesting Product Line inside Territory puts a subtotal for each product line within each territory. Grouping by Product Line and then Territory nests the other way round, subtotalling each territory within each product line. Sorting orders the rows but creates no group footers, so there are no subtotals. A prompt leaves the choice of product line to whoever runs the report.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Ships and Trains

questions.scenario: A product manager exploring a sales cube in Analyzer wants to reshape and extend the analysis without asking IT for help.
questions.prompt: Which two of these can they do directly in the analysis?
options: Drill from Years down to Quarters
Add a new level to the Time hierarchy
Create a calculated measure from Sales
Rewrite the SQL that Mondrian generates
Correct order rows in the fact table
questions.explanation: Drilling a hierarchy and creating a calculated measure are both analysis actions: each edits the report's MDX query. Analyzer reads the cube and never writes to the fact table. Hierarchy levels are defined in the Mondrian schema, so a new level is a modelling change. Mondrian generates the SQL from MDX, and users do not edit it.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — OLAP & Mondrian

questions.scenario: An analyst viewing Sales by Years double-clicks the 2003 column header, and it expands into QTR1 to QTR4 while every other field stays the same.
questions.prompt: What is this operation called?
options: Drill-through
Pivot
Slice
Drill-down
questions.explanation: Drill-down moves from one level of a hierarchy to the level below it, here Years to Quarters, keeping the rest of the view. Drill-through opens the detail rows behind a cell. A pivot moves fields between rows and columns. A slice restricts a dimension to chosen members.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Drill-down

questions.scenario: A sales manager wants each cell in a Quantity column to show a bar whose length reflects its value, so the largest countries stand out without reading the numbers.
questions.prompt: Which conditional formatting should be applied to Quantity?
options: Data Bar
Trend Arrow
Color Scale
Heat grid
questions.explanation: A Data Bar draws a bar in each cell sized to its value, which is exactly a comparison by length. A Color Scale shades cell backgrounds by value, so it compares by colour rather than length. A Trend Arrow shows the direction of change, not magnitude. A heat grid is a chart type that replaces the table rather than formatting a column in it.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Conditional formatting

questions.scenario: Management wants to see at a glance which countries in a territory account for the largest share of the quantity sold in one year.
questions.prompt: Which visualisation suits this best?
options: Tree map
Line chart
Scatter chart
Heat grid
questions.explanation: A tree map sizes each rectangle by its value within the whole, so the biggest contributors stand out at a glance. A line chart shows change along an ordered axis such as time, not share. A scatter chart plots two measures against each other to show a relationship. A heat grid colours cells across two dimensions, which compares values but does not show each country's share of the total.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Visualisations

questions.scenario: The nightly load added yesterday's orders to the sales fact table, but an analysis that had been run before the load still shows the old totals after it is refreshed.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: Analyzer only sends a new query when the layout changes
Mondrian is serving cell values it cached before the load
The browser is showing a cached copy of the earlier page
The saved analysis stored its results along with its layout
questions.explanation: Mondrian keeps a cache of cell values, shared across users, so cells it already holds are served without new SQL; Administration > Clear Cache flushes it and the new rows appear. A saved analysis holds a report definition, not results. A browser refresh fetches the page again, and the stale figures come from the server. Analyzer sends a query whenever the report runs; it is the cache that answers it.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Administration

questions.scenario: A cube models Country, State and City as three separate dimensions instead of one Markets hierarchy, and users complain that double-clicking a country does not show its cities.
questions.prompt: Why does this design block the drill?
options: Analyzer supports drill-down only on the Time dimension
Cities must first be added as a filter before drilling
Drill-down works only once drill-through links have been enabled
Drill-down follows one hierarchy's levels, and none links them
questions.explanation: Double-clicking asks Mondrian for a member's children, and those exist only when the schema defines the levels in one hierarchy, such as Country > State > City. Any hierarchy can be drilled, not only Time. Drill-through links show detail rows and are a separate option from drill-down. A filter restricts members; it does not create the parent-child link a drill needs.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Hierarchies

questions.scenario: Margin % is needed in a dozen Analyzer reports and two dashboards, and finance insists it is calculated identically everywhere.
questions.prompt: Where should Margin % be defined?
options: As a user-defined measure in each Analyzer report
As a calculated field in an Interactive Report
As a calculated member in the Mondrian schema
In a spreadsheet, after exporting the data to CSV
questions.explanation: A calculated member declared in the schema is available to every report on the cube with one definition and one format, so every consumer computes it the same way. A user-defined measure lives in one report's definition, so a dozen copies can drift apart. An Interactive Report calculated field serves only that report and cannot be aggregated. Exporting to a spreadsheet takes the calculation out of the governed model entirely.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Calculated measures

questions.scenario: A manager sees an unexpectedly high Sales figure for one territory, product line and quarter, and wants to see the individual order lines behind it.
questions.prompt: What should be enabled in the analysis?
options: Drill-through links on measure cells, in Report Options
Subtotals on the Territory level, with Show Subtotals
A Rank user-defined measure on the Sales column
Drill-down on the Quarters level of the Time hierarchy
questions.explanation: Showing drill-through links on measure cells, in Report Options, turns each non-calculated measure into a link that returns the fact rows behind that cell. Drill-down moves to finer levels such as months but still shows aggregates. Subtotals add summary rows, not detail. A rank orders members; it does not reveal the rows behind a figure.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Drill-through

questions.scenario: An analysis filtered to three EMEA countries shows a Territory subtotal set to Aggregate. A colleague expected it to match the cube's full EMEA figure, but it is lower.
questions.prompt: Why is the subtotal lower than the full EMEA figure?
options: Totals are visual by default, covering only members left after filters
Subtotals leave out every member whose value is blank rather than zero
Aggregate averages the visible cells instead of adding them all together
The cube caches EMEA figures only at the country level of the hierarchy
questions.explanation: By default Analyzer uses visual totals, so the Aggregate is recomputed over the countries left after the filter; a Report Options setting makes totals include the filtered members and return the cube's full EMEA value. Aggregate asks Mondrian for the parent's own cell using the measure's aggregator; it does not average. The cache stores cell values and does not change what a total covers. Blank versus zero affects averages, not which members a total covers.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Totals

questions.scenario: An analyst drags Territory to rows and Years to columns, and an administrator then opens the analysis log to see what ran.
questions.prompt: What does the log show that Analyzer sent to Mondrian?
options: A request to reload the cube from its tables
An MDX query, which Mondrian turned into SQL
A SQL query that Analyzer wrote directly
An MQL query against a metadata model
questions.explanation: Analyzer's language is MDX: each gesture edits the report and sends MDX to Mondrian, which translates it into SQL against the fact and dimension tables, and the log shows the MDX and its timing. Analyzer never writes SQL itself. MQL is the metadata query language behind Interactive Reports and Dashboard Designer queries. Nothing is reloaded; Mondrian queries on demand and caches the cells.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — OLAP & Mondrian

questions.scenario: A designer is building a sales dashboard and wants to combine existing content with new visuals in its panels.
questions.prompt: Which three of these can be placed in a panel?
options: A PDI transformation canvas
An Analyzer report from the repository
A web page, shown by its URL
A Mondrian schema, opened for editing
A chart built in Chart Designer
questions.explanation: A panel can show Interactive Reporting, Analyzer and Report Designer content from the repository, charts built in Chart Designer, data tables, and a web page by its URL. A PDI transformation canvas belongs to Spoon, a desktop tool, and is not dashboard content. A Mondrian schema is edited in Schema Workbench; a dashboard can show reports built on it, not the schema itself.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Overview

questions.scenario: A designer adds a Territory prompt to a dashboard, but the orders report in one panel offers no parameter to associate it with, so the report ignores the selection.
questions.prompt: What must change for the prompt to filter that report?
options: The panel must have content linking enabled on its Territory field
The prompt must take its values from a Metadata List
The dashboard must be saved before the prompt can apply
The report's Territory filter must be defined as a parameter
questions.explanation: A dashboard prompt can be applied to a report only when the report's filter is set up as a parameter; the association then maps the prompt onto that parameter. A Metadata List only supplies the prompt's values and gives the report no parameter. Content linking publishes clicks from a panel; it does not give a report a parameter to receive. Saving matters for content linking, and an unmapped report ignores the prompt whether or not the dashboard is saved.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Filters & content linking

questions.scenario: A dashboard chart is meant to compare only the product lines beginning with M, but its query returns every row of a large inventory table, and the panel loads slowly.
questions.prompt: Which change will do most to speed it up?
options: Add a Product Line condition to the chart's query
Switch the dashboard to a lighter visual theme
Give the chart a larger panel in the layout
Set a shorter refresh interval on the dashboard
questions.explanation: A condition in the query is rendered into the SQL's WHERE clause, so the database returns only the rows the chart needs, and the chart only ever sees the query's result. A theme changes colours, not how much data is fetched. A larger panel changes the drawing area, not the query. A shorter refresh interval runs the same slow query more often.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Inventory

questions.scenario: A team needs a quick inventory table on a dashboard, and no report exists for it. A colleague suggests building and publishing an Interactive Report first, to place in the panel.
questions.prompt: What is the more direct option?
options: Insert a Data Table panel that queries the inventory model
Insert a URL panel that points straight at the inventory database
Wait for IT to publish a report built in Report Designer
Export the inventory to CSV and place the file in a panel
questions.explanation: Dashboard Designer can build data tables and charts straight from a data source with a metadata query, with no report needed first, which is what query-based panels are for. A URL panel shows a web page and cannot query a database. Waiting for a published report is the slow route a query-based panel avoids. A CSV export is a static copy that goes stale, and a panel shows content, not raw files.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Inventory

questions.scenario: In a three-panel dashboard, clicking a product in an Analyzer report updates a pie chart of territory sales, and clicking a territory in the pie updates a bar chart of order status for that product and territory.
questions.prompt: Which panels re-run their queries when a user clicks a territory in the pie chart?
options: Only the bar chart
The pie chart and the bar chart
All three, starting with the report
None, until the dashboard is refreshed
questions.explanation: The bar chart is the only panel that takes its territory from the pie, so a click on the pie re-runs the bar chart alone; a click on the report would re-run the pie and then the bar, since both take the product from it. The pie publishes the territory; it does not re-query itself when clicked. The Analyzer report subscribes to nothing, so no click in another panel reaches it. Content linking acts on the click itself, with no manual refresh.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Product Performance

questions.scenario: A designer enables content linking on the Product field of an Analyzer panel, but no other panel changes yet when a product is clicked.
questions.prompt: What has enabling content linking done so far?
options: Made the panel publish the clicked product as a parameter
Added a Product prompt to the dashboard's prompt toolbar
Filtered every panel on the dashboard by the product
Linked the panel to every chart that has a Product column
questions.explanation: Enabling content linking declares an output parameter that the panel emits on each click; nothing reacts until another panel maps one of its parameters to that output. It filters nothing by itself. Prompts in the toolbar are created separately, in the Prompts area. Panels are never linked automatically by matching column names; each link is an explicit parameter mapping.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Content linking

questions.scenario: Managers using a sales dashboard must be able to pick one or more territories with a single click each, and the list must stay in step with the data as territories are added.
questions.prompt: Which prompt set-up meets both needs?
options: Text field, values typed in by the user, multiple selections allowed
Buttons, values from a static list, one selection only
Buttons, values from a Metadata List, multiple selections allowed
Drop-down, values from a Metadata List, one selection only
questions.explanation: Buttons select with one click each, a Metadata List queries the model for the current Territory values so the list keeps up with the data, and allowing multiple selections lets a manager pick several. A drop-down over a Metadata List keeps the values current, but one selection only blocks picking several territories. A text field makes users type values, which invites mismatches. Buttons over a static single-select list fail on both counts: the list has to be edited by hand when territories change, and only one can be picked.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Vendor Sales

questions.scenario: A dashboard needs one panel showing each territory's share of total sales, and another showing how monthly sales have moved over two years.
questions.prompt: Which pair of Chart Designer chart types fits best?
options: A pie chart for the share, a dial chart for the trend
A pie chart for the share, a line chart for the trend
A dial chart for the share, a pie chart for the trend
A line chart for the share, a pie chart for the trend
questions.explanation: A pie shows the parts of a whole, which is exactly each territory's share of total sales, and a line shows change along an ordered time axis. A line chart for the share draws unordered territories as if they were a sequence, and a pie chart for the trend hides the order of the months. A dial shows one value against a scale, so it can show neither several territories' shares nor a trend.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Chart selection

questions.scenario: A chart's query has the condition Product Name = {PRODUCT} with a default value, and PRODUCT is mapped to clicks in another panel.
questions.prompt: What does the chart show when the dashboard first opens, before anyone clicks?
options: Every product's figures, until a product is clicked
Figures for the default product, until a click replaces it
An error, because PRODUCT does not have a value yet
An empty chart, until a product has been clicked
questions.explanation: The default fills the parameter when the dashboard opens, so the query runs with the default product until a click supplies another value. The condition always applies, so the chart never falls back to every product. It is not empty, because the default gives the condition a value. No error arises, for the same reason.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Product Performance

questions.scenario: A designer maps a chart's PRODUCT parameter to an Analyzer panel's Product output, then clicks a product in the not-yet-saved dashboard, and the chart does not change.
questions.prompt: What should they do first?
options: Add a Product prompt to the prompt toolbar
Enable drill-through links in the Analyzer report
Save the dashboard, then test the link again
Rebuild the chart's query against the cube
questions.explanation: Content linking works only once the dashboard has been saved, so an unsaved dashboard ignores the click even when the mapping is right. A toolbar prompt is a separate way to set a parameter and does not activate the link. Drill-through links show detail rows inside Analyzer and have nothing to do with publishing a click to other panels. The chart's metadata query is fine as it is; the parameter mapping is the only link between the panels.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Content linking
